metadata.title: Prophet Abraham (pbuh) A1 — Teacher Guide
metadata.subtitle: 9 short lessons with chapter-specific support, grammar found in the story, and 30-minute lesson plans
metadata.estimatedDuration: 9 chapter lessons of about 30 minutes each, plus one 40-minute review lesson for the end pages.
metadata.targetAudience: A1 English learners: young beginners (Years 2–4) and adult beginners.
metadata.targetLearners: Learners who can read very short, simple sentences with pictures, sentence frames and help from the teacher.
metadata.purpose: Develop A1 reading, listening, speaking and writing through the story of Prophet Abraham (pbuh): the stone gods, the fire, the journey, Zamzam and the Ka’ba.
metadata.approachDesc: Route in every chapter: Before You Read → Listen → Read → Quick Challenge → Language Focus (Look → Practise → Use) → I can. Grammar is found in the story first. Learners notice the form in a story sentence, then use it about their own life.

readingFramework.before: Before You Read: one picture or one guess question.
readingFramework.during: The audio for A1 is not ready yet: read the chapter aloud yourself, slowly, twice. Then learners read and do one small task (underline, columns, act).
readingFramework.after: Quick Challenge, then Language Focus (Look → Practise → Use), then I can and an exit ticket.

cefrProfile.intro: This book is written for CEFR A1. The table shows the A1 descriptors of the CEFR Companion Volume (2020) that the tasks are built on. Vocabulary (English Vocabulary Profile): learners see only A1 words, words with a Word Note and words from the story. Instruction words that the app uses in every book (match, order, true, false, chapter) are taught once in the first lesson. Grammar (English Grammar Profile): past simple affirmative, was / were, can, because and there is / there are are A1. Did not, could not, past questions, will and there was / there were are A2. The story uses them, so learners meet them in the text and choose them in exercises. Free use is only expected with sentence frames. Türkiye Century Maarif Model English Curriculum (Years 2–8): “CEFR level A1 has been adapted as A1.1, A1.2, A1.3 in Years 2, 3 and 4 for Primary Education.” The grammar route follows the Year 4 (Level A1.3) “Target Language Chunks in Use”: “To be” in the past (was, were), “There was/ There were”, “The Simple Past Tense (+) (-) (?)” with regular and irregular verbs, and wh- question words. Imperatives are in Year 2, Theme 1. The curriculum’s learning outcomes are written for its own themes. This book is a supplementary reader, so it supports these language chunks but does not cover a theme’s outcomes. Young learners (Years 2–4): the curriculum says “There is no analysis or teaching of grammatical structures at this stage.” With children, teach each Language Focus as chunks: say, repeat, act and play. Do not read the Explanation lines to them. The Explanation lines are for adult beginners and for self-study.

rows.descriptor: Can understand very short, simple texts a single phrase at a time, picking up familiar names, words and basic phrases and rereading as required.
practice: Before You Read and Quick Challenge in every chapter.

rows.descriptor: Can ask and answer simple questions, initiate and respond to simple statements in areas of immediate need or on very familiar topics.
practice: Chapter 3: ask a partner “Did you … yesterday?”

rows.descriptor: Can produce simple, mainly isolated phrases about people and places.
practice: Chapter 1: say what a stone cannot do.
Chapter 7: say what you will do tomorrow.

rows.descriptor: Can give information about matters of personal relevance (e.g. likes and dislikes, family, pets) using simple words/signs and basic expressions. Can produce simple isolated phrases and sentences.
practice: Chapter 9: write about a job you do together.

rows.descriptor: Can understand instructions addressed carefully and slowly to them and follow short, simple directions.
practice: Instruction check questions in every chapter (Classroom management).

sensitiveNotes.title: Source fidelity and respectful teaching
notes: Never draw or show Prophet Abraham (pbuh), Ishmael (pbuh) or any prophet. Nimrod is shown only as a symbol.
In Chapter 1, Abraham plays with the stone gods. Explain that this shows they were only stones; do not ask learners to act it out.
Chapter 4: keep the focus on Allah’s help. Do not act out the fire.
Do not add legends, dates or details that are not in this A1 book.

grammarSequence: Chapter 1: Past forms (was, called, did not know); could not + verb.
Chapter 2: Past forms (saw, went away, knew); yes/no questions with be: “Is this my god?”
Chapter 3: Past questions: “Who broke our gods?”, “Did you do this?”; can for ability (EGP: past wh- and did questions are A2, so learners understand them in the story and ask them with frames).
Chapter 4: because for reasons; was not + adjective (afraid, safe).
Chapter 5: can / cannot for ability now; could not for the past.
Chapter 6: Past travel verbs (left, traveled, came); there was / there were.
Chapter 7: will + verb for the future; there was no / there were no.
Chapter 8: Regular and irregular past (shouted, lived / came, drank, gave); present for today (“This water is very famous today”).
Chapter 9: will + verb (“You will help me.” “I will help you.”); together.

sections.title: 1. Make Your Plan
sections.text: This book has 9 short chapters. One chapter takes about 15 minutes.
points: Before each chapter, read its “I can” lines.

sections.title: 2. Every Chapter: 4 Steps
sections.text: Do the same four steps in every chapter.
points: Look and guess: Look at the picture. Answer “Before You Read”.
Read: Read the chapter two times. Read it aloud one time.
Words: Tap the bold words. Say each word two times.
Check: Do the Quick Challenge and the Language Focus. Then read “I can”. Can you do it?

sections.title: 3. Look Back
sections.text: At the end of the book:
points: Do the end pages: Knowledge Check, Vocabulary Challenge, Language Review, Final Challenge.
